title: Meningitis Signs: Neck Stiffness, Kernig and Brudzinski
subject: Medical Triads
preview: Meningeal irritation may produce neck stiffness, photophobia and headache, but bedside signs are not sensitive enough to exclude meningitis.
quickRevision: Meningeal irritation may produce neck stiffness, photophobia and headache, but bedside signs are not sensitive enough to exclude meningitis.
Altered consciousness, seizures, petechial rash or hemodynamic instability signal higher urgency.
Prompt clinical assessment and appropriate treatment matter; lumbar puncture decisions account for safety and contraindications.

sections.title: Recognize the pattern
points: Meningeal irritation may produce neck stiffness, photophobia and headache, but bedside signs are not sensitive enough to exclude meningitis.
Kernig and Brudzinski signs are classic examination findings; their absence does not reliably rule out disease.

sections.title: What this finding does—and does not—mean
points: Altered consciousness, seizures, petechial rash or hemodynamic instability signal higher urgency.
Prompt clinical assessment and appropriate treatment matter; lumbar puncture decisions account for safety and contraindications.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not delay urgent antimicrobials in a severely unwell patient solely to obtain a textbook-perfect sign.

quiz.question: What is the limitation of a negative Kernig sign?
quiz.explanation: It does not exclude meningitis. Meningeal irritation may produce neck stiffness, photophobia and headache, but bedside signs are not sensitive enough to exclude meningitis.
